families.name: After 1.e4 e5
families.blurb: Both sides grab the middle. The oldest games of all.

families.name: Answers to 1.e4
families.blurb: What to play when they push the king pawn.

families.name: After 1.d4
families.blurb: The quieter start. Plans instead of fireworks.

families.name: From the side
families.blurb: Take the middle later, with pieces.

openings.name: The Italian Game
openings.idea: Point your bishop straight at f7, the weakest square near their king.
openings.when: Your first opening as White. Everything you want happens naturally.
openings.famous: Every beginner starts here. So did most world champions.
openings.meet: Copy it. Bishop to c5 and you both have the same good squares.

trap.name: Legal's Mate
trap.say: White gives up the queen. Three moves later it is checkmate with two knights and a bishop.

openings.name: The Ruy Lopez
openings.idea: Annoy the knight that guards their e5 pawn, then build slowly behind it.
openings.when: After the Italian feels easy. It rewards patience rather than tricks.
openings.famous: The favourite of Lasker, Capablanca, Fischer, Kasparov and Carlsen.
openings.meet: Push the bishop with a6, then take the middle with your own pieces.

openings.name: The Scotch Game
openings.idea: Open the middle at once so every piece has somewhere to go.
openings.when: You like pieces out fast and you do not want a long slow game.
openings.famous: Kasparov brought it back at the very top in the 1990s.
openings.meet: Take on d4 and develop. Nothing is wrong with your position.

openings.name: The King's Gambit
openings.idea: Give a pawn away on move two to rip the middle open.
openings.when: For fun, and for learning attack. It is genuinely risky.
openings.famous: Morphy and the players of the 1800s lived on this.
openings.meet: Take the pawn, then give it back later to finish developing.

trap.name: The Kieseritzky
trap.say: Black holds the pawn with g5 and h4 breaks the chain. The knight lands on e5 and the game is wide open.

openings.name: The Vienna Game
openings.idea: Develop the knight first, then push the f pawn like a gambit anyway.
openings.when: You want the King’s Gambit without the danger on move two.
openings.famous: Steinitz, the first world champion, played it as White.
openings.meet: Answer f4 with d5 in the middle. Never take the f pawn straight away.

openings.name: The Evans Gambit
openings.idea: Give a pawn to gain time, then build a huge pawn centre with c3 and d4.
openings.when: Once the Italian is second nature and you want to attack.
openings.famous: Morphy’s weapon. Kasparov used it to win in 25 moves in 1995.
openings.meet: Take the pawn, give it back at the right moment, and finish developing.

openings.name: The Petrov
openings.idea: Copy them. Instead of defending the pawn, attack theirs.
openings.when: You want a safe game as Black and you do not mind a quiet one.
openings.famous: Kramnik used it to hold the very strongest players to draws.
openings.meet: Take on e5, but be ready to retreat before you win anything.

trap.name: The copycat that goes wrong
trap.say: Copying one move too long loses the queen. Play d6 first and kick the knight away.

openings.name: The Sicilian Defence
openings.idea: Do not copy them. Trade a side pawn for a middle one and play for a win.
openings.when: When a draw is no good to you. It is sharp: learn it slowly.
openings.famous: Tal, Fischer, Kasparov, Anand, Carlsen. The champions’ defence.
openings.meet: Open the middle with d4, take back with the knight, and castle quickly.

openings.name: The French Defence
openings.idea: Build a wall of pawns, let them have space, then hit the bottom of the wall.
openings.when: You like solid positions and you do not mind a cramped start.
openings.famous: Alekhine, Botvinnik and Petrosian all leaned on it.
openings.meet: Push past with e5 and take the space. Attack on the king side.

openings.name: The Caro-Kann
openings.idea: Like the French, but the light bishop gets out first. Nothing is left stuck.
openings.when: You want the safest answer to 1.e4 there is.
openings.famous: Karpov made a career of it. Carlsen still plays it.
openings.meet: Take the middle with d4 and play for the extra space.

openings.name: The Scandinavian
openings.idea: Challenge the middle on move one and get the queen out early on purpose.
openings.when: Your first defence as Black. There is almost nothing to remember.
openings.famous: The oldest recorded opening in chess, from 1475.
openings.meet: Hit the queen with Nc3, gaining time while you develop.

trap.name: The bishop that walks into a net
trap.say: The bishop is chased to g6 and then boxed in. Play Bxf3 or Bd7 instead and it stays free.

openings.name: The Queen's Gambit
openings.idea: Offer a wing pawn to drag their middle pawn away from the middle.
openings.when: Your first opening after 1.d4. Every plan is about the centre.
openings.famous: Lasker and Capablanca both defended it as Black for years.
openings.meet: Decline it with e6 or c6. You do not have to take the pawn.

trap.name: Hanging on to the pawn
trap.say: Trying to keep the extra pawn with b5 loses a rook to Qf3. Give the pawn back and develop.

openings.name: The Slav Defence
openings.idea: Hold the middle with c6 so the light bishop still has a way out.
openings.when: The solid answer to 1.d4, and easier than it looks.
openings.famous: Euwe and Smyslov both used it to become world champion.
openings.meet: Play a4 to stop them keeping the pawn, then finish developing.

openings.name: The King's Indian
openings.idea: Let them build a huge centre. Then blow it up with your own pawns.
openings.when: For later. It needs nerve and it needs a plan.
openings.famous: Fischer, Tal and Kasparov used it to win with Black.
openings.meet: Take the space, castle, and be ready for their king side push.

openings.name: The London System
openings.idea: Build the same safe house every single game, whatever they do.
openings.when: You want one setup you never have to think about.
openings.famous: Carlsen plays it at the top, which surprised everyone.
openings.meet: Play c5 early and hit the d4 pawn before the house is finished.

openings.name: The English Opening
openings.idea: Take the middle from the side, with a pawn on c4 and a bishop on g2.
openings.when: You would rather squeeze than attack.
openings.famous: Botvinnik, Smyslov and Kramnik all used it as their main move.
openings.meet: Answer with e5 and treat it like a Sicilian with colours swapped.

openings.name: The Réti
openings.idea: Do not touch the middle yet. Aim at it from a distance and strike later.
openings.when: The newest idea here, and the hardest to play well.
openings.famous: Gukesh, the youngest world champion, opens with it.
openings.meet: Take the middle with pawns while they are still pointing at it.
